About

Build it, test it, ship it, and never stop learning.

I didn't end up here by accident. Over two years of building software end to end: backend architecture, databases, and the interfaces that sit on top of them. None of it happened without second-guessing myself, without nights spent working out why a test kept failing, without rewriting a specification three times before it finally held up. A Master's degree in computer systems later, that is the standard I hold myself to: I don't accept a product that only more or less works.

What I love about this field is how many different things it asks of you. Project management teaches me to structure and to anticipate. Web development lets me build something concrete where nothing existed before. UI/UX pushes me to sit in the place of the person who will actually use the product, not just to make it run. And testing, the part everyone skips and I never do, is what proves the rest of the work holds up once it ships.

Today, as an Assistant Project Manager at Kyo Conseil, I coordinate delivery with the same rigour I would have applied building it myself, and I still build: as a freelance full-stack web developer for Olten Agency. Because underneath it all, the same question keeps driving me: does this actually work, and could someone else pick it up and understand it after me?
